About the role:

You will be a core contributor on a small, high-ownership engineering team. That means working across the full stack, taking features from design to production, and being someone the team genuinely relies on, technically and otherwise.

Day to day, this includes:

  • Building new features on both the customer-facing platform and the internal tools our analysts use to produce intelligence.

  • Designing and maintaining the APIs that power our product.

  • Contributing to our AI initiatives, not just integrating models, but thinking carefully about where AI genuinely adds value in our product.

  • Participating in architecture decisions and technical discussions, not just executing them.

  • Reviewing code with the goal of making the whole team better, not just catching bugs.

  • Staying curious about new tools and approaches, and bringing that curiosity to the team.

Your first 90 days:

Week 1 — You spend your first week getting up to speed. That means onboarding sessions to understand our business, our clients, and what we are building, alongside setting up your environment and getting familiar with the codebase. You will likely ship something small by the end of the week, but the goal is to build a solid foundation, not to prove anything yet.

Weeks 2 to 4 — You start contributing independently, picking up bugs and small improvements that let you navigate the codebase with growing confidence. By the end of the month, you are working on your first real feature, customer-facing, with enough scope to be meaningful.

Days 30 to 90 — You become a full contributor. You take ownership of features, deliver them without needing hand-holding, and your code reviews are genuinely useful to the team. You have internalized our standards well enough that you are reinforcing them, not learning them. You are autonomous on most technical topics, even if some corners of the codebase are still new to you.

By day 90, we know we can give you something and trust that it will get done well.

What we are looking for:

You have solid experience building production-grade applications, enough that you know what good looks like and why it matters. You are comfortable with ambiguity, can navigate a codebase that is still evolving, and take ownership without needing to be managed.

More specifically:

  • Strong command of TypeScript, React, NestJS and GraphQL. You know these well enough to have opinions about them.

  • Experience with relational databases and data modeling (we use PostgreSQL via Prisma).

  • Comfortable with Docker, CI/CD, and automated testing as part of your normal workflow, not as an afterthought.

  • You write code for the next person who will read it, not just for today’s deadline.

  • Fluent in English, written and spoken. Our team and documentation are in English.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with workflow automation tools (we use n8n extensively).

  • Familiarity with LLM tooling or AI integration in production contexts.

  • Experience in a startup or small team environment where you wore multiple hats.

Recruitment process:

  • Intro call with a Talent Acquisition Specialist (15-20 mins).

  • Interview with our Tech Lead (1h).

  • Case Study (take home test, 3 days to complete)

  • Final interview with 2 members of the leadership team and coffee chat with the team.

  • Reference check

Where Europe's enterprises adopt AI

Langdock is the AI platform used by more than 10,000 companies to give employees secure access to the leading AI models, to build and share agents and to automate repetitive workflows. We have grown past $40M ARR while remaining a small team, and we care deeply about operating efficiently across the entire company.

For many enterprises, Langdock is becoming the place where most of the net-new work is produced. As people and agents create more documents, analyses, decisions, and automations inside AI interfaces, the context and data behind that work accumulate within Langdock. This gives us the opportunity to earn a larger role in their technology stack by building a platform they choose to rely on.

Our ambition is to build that platform for European enterprises while preserving their control over data, model providers, and deployment environments. We have made meaningful progress at the application layer, but much of the foundation beneath it still needs to be built.

You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

The role

Distributed Systems Engineers solve our most complex technical problems inside and across Langdock's shared services when existing building blocks or standard architectures are insufficient. These are problems where correctness under failure, performance, scale, security, and cost interact.

This is a project-oriented role rather than ownership of one permanent layer. You might spend a period on distributed execution, then move into storage architecture, workload isolation, or model serving as company priorities change. The constant is sustained investigation of unfamiliar systems and responsibility for turning that understanding into a production system.

Systems Engineers own the difficult mechanism and the measurable improvement it creates, whether in correctness, capability, performance, reliability, or cost. They operate what they build, while the Platform owner remains accountable for the service contract and long-term lifecycle around it.

What you might work on

The systems agenda includes:

  • Distributed state and execution. Design systems that remain correct when work is concurrent, long-running, retried, resumed, or moved between processes. Define explicit invariants for ordering, idempotency, recovery, and tenant isolation.

  • Storage and data systems. Improve how large volumes of customer and agent-generated data are stored, versioned, moved, and recovered while preserving consistency, data residency, and predictable performance.

  • Secure compute for agents. Develop the isolation, runtime, and scheduling mechanisms behind a shared sandbox service for untrusted code. The system needs persistent filesystems, deny-by-default networking, scoped mounts, fast startup, suspension, resumption, and predictable scheduling without weakening the security boundary.

  • Inference systems. Improve the serving systems beneath the Model Gateway, optimizing throughput, latency, accelerator utilization, reliability, and cost. The work is measurement driven: understand the workload, identify the actual bottleneck, and decide where changes to serving, scheduling, caching, model format, or hardware create structural advantage.

  • Resource scheduling and isolation. Make CPU, memory, storage, network, and accelerator capacity explicit so one workload cannot degrade another. Improve placement, admission control, backpressure, autoscaling, and recovery across deployment environments.

  • Billing and usage metering. Build the concurrent metering mechanism behind the billing capability, accounting for heterogeneous units such as model tokens and sandbox compute time. It must stay correct when many workloads report concurrently, events arrive late or more than once, and long-running jobs reserve capacity before their final usage is known. This involves idempotent ingestion, atomic reservations, reconciliation, and auditable records.

You will start with one focused problem based on your experience and the team's priorities. The expectation is not broad activity across every domain; it is a substantial improvement in the capability, performance, reliability, or economics of the system you take on.

Tech stack

  • Go and TypeScript in one Bazel monorepo, with implementation choices driven by the system

  • Linux, containers, microVMs, filesystems, and networking

  • Protobuf and gRPC for service contracts

  • Kubernetes across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on-premises deployments

  • Terraform and Terragrunt for infrastructure orchestration

  • PostgreSQL and Redis where durable metadata or coordination requires them

  • Open-source model serving and accelerator infrastructure

You do not need prior experience with every item. You do need enough systems depth to enter an unfamiliar part of the stack, understand its behavior, and make consequential changes safely.

How we work

  • We operate with high trust and autonomy in squads of 3 to 4 engineers. A squad owns its roadmap, prioritization, technical decisions, and operation in production. Engineers are expected to find the context they need, ask for input when it improves the outcome, and move work forward without waiting for every next step to be assigned.

  • We align asynchronously before scheduling a meeting. Product requirement documents (PRDs) define the user problem, intended outcome, and constraints. Design documents make architectural boundaries, tradeoffs, failure modes, migrations, and rollouts explicit. People read and challenge the thinking asynchronously; once the context is shared, a short in-office discussion or whiteboard session usually resolves the remaining questions quickly.

  • We optimize for leverage. Engineers choose the AI tools that work for them, supported by clear ticket context, focused branches, automated tests, and AI review before human review. We also invest in observability, migration tooling, automated recovery, and runbooks so recurring product maintenance does not depend on someone remembering a manual step.

  • The engineer who ships a change owns it in production. If something breaks, you lead the fix.

What we are looking for

  • You have owned technically difficult production systems in areas such as distributed systems, databases, runtimes, inference, networking, or storage. You operate what you build and remain responsible for it after deployment.

  • You reason from first principles, form testable hypotheses, and use measurement to understand unfamiliar behavior. You investigate beyond the first working solution until you understand the underlying mechanism.

  • Given an underspecified problem, you identify the most important invariant, decide where depth will change the outcome, and defend what you deliberately leave out.

  • You reason precisely about concurrency, isolation, ordering, data loss, and failure, while finding pragmatic ways to improve performance, reliability, or cost without unnecessary complexity.

  • You use AI tools as leverage while verifying their output and retaining ownership of the result. You communicate complex systems clearly, expose uncertainty, and work constructively with others.

This is an experienced individual-contributor role. You should be able to independently investigate an unfamiliar problem, design a solution, ship it, and operate it in production. We generally expect this judgment to come from at least three to six six of full-time experience working on production systems.

Working here

This is an in-office role at Greifswalder Strasse 212 in Berlin. We work together in person because it helps us build trust, develop shared context, and make decisions quickly.

Most engineers start around 8:30. We usually eat lunch together, and dinner is available for people who stay later. Running and gym are part of the routine for many of us.

Join one of the highest-rated workplaces on Glassdoor and experience what it means to thrive in a truly remote-first world.

As a Senior PHP/Symfony Engineer, you will take hands-on ownership of backend development within a mature Symfony platform that manages marketing and revenue data for enterprise customers. The core application currently runs on Symfony 6.1, with an upgrade to Symfony 7 planned, alongside an Angular front end and TypeScript and Python AI agent microservices.

  • 3+ years of recent commercial experience with Symfony 6.x/7 at Advanced level. Strong senior-level Laravel experience may be considered where the experience is clearly transferable and the candidate has a good understanding of the differences between Laravel and Symfony.

  • 2+ years of Advanced experience using AI development tools critically, including reviewing, validating and challenging AI-generated code rather than accepting it without question.

  • At least 1 year of experience working with or understanding Angular/TypeScript. Experience with React or Vue using TypeScript may also be considered, but some front-end exposure is essential.
  • 3+ years of Advanced experience with automated testing using PHPUnit. Experience with Pest or another equivalent PHP testing framework may also be considered.
  • At least 1 year of Intermediate experience working on framework upgrades and modernising legacy codebases. Experience with major-version upgrades or significant refactoring in other large PHP applications may be considered.
  • 2+ years of Intermediate AWS experience. Equivalent experience with Azure or GCP may also be considered.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to work effectively in a remote environment.
  • Ability to work UK hours.
  • Ability to successfully complete strict background checks and adhere to PII and data protection requirements.
  • Strong self-sufficiency, with the ability to operate independently and without handholding after 2–3 months, while continuing to collaborate effectively with the wider team.
  • A hands-on engineering approach combined with an architectural mindset, with the ability to understand how and why the wider system works rather than focusing only on writing code.

Nice to Have

  • 2+ years of Intermediate CI/CD experience with GitHub Actions; GitLab CI, Jenkins or Azure DevOps are suitable alternatives.

  • Partneranbindungen & Integrationen: Lösungsevaluierung, Umsetzung und Dokumentation von Schnittstellen zu Partner- und Drittsystemen.

Dein Profil

Technisch

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung mit PHP & Laravel: Entwicklung von Webanwendungen über den gesamten Stack, im Frontend idealerweise mit Livewire, Alpine.js, Flux UI und Tailwind CSS.

About Us

STARK is a defence technology company redefining the engineering and deployment of autonomous platforms. Our core mission is to deliver fully operational unmanned systems, integrating the critical subsystems, including Electronic Warfare, necessary for NATO forces to maintain a decisive advantage in contested environments. We do whatever is required to achieve platform autonomy, grounded in precision, responsibility, and uncompromising engineering discipline.


About the team

We are a lean, agile group with a strong systems-minded focus. We operate without silos, looking for proactive engineers who are excited to take mathematical models off the whiteboard and deploy them onto physical hardware. On our Electronic Warfare algorithms team, you will bridge the gap between theoretical signal processing and real-world hardware execution, taking direct ownership of key software and firmware modules.


Your mission

At STARK, we are building the next generation of autonomous platforms capable of navigating the world's most contested environments. As a Senior Mesh Network and MAC Engineer you will solve the critical challenges of directional wireless communication in highly dynamic networks. You will design and implement the medium access control (MAC) and routing layers that allow our platforms to form robust, self-healing networks under demanding tactical conditions.


Responsibilities

  • Architect and implement MAC protocols and routing algorithms tailored for directional multi-node systems, directly tackling the challenge of neighbour discovery under highly focused, narrow beams.
  • Build dynamic TDMA schedules and beam coordination mechanisms in lockstep with the physical layer (PHY) and antenna steering systems, ensuring routing decisions are grounded in real-time RF characteristics rather than simple hop counts.
  • Deliver resilient multi-hop relay capabilities that sustain high-bandwidth video and control links between mobile platforms over tactical distances, routing back seamlessly to ground control stations under dynamic conditions.
  • Build and maintain multi-node Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testbeds alongside automated logging pipelines to quantitatively evaluate and verify network join times and topology reform behaviours.
  • Mesh networking in a product that shipped — sim work alone does not qualify — plus Linux networking at kernel and packet level with live debugging.
  • Radio-literate and has designed a medium-access scheme or TDMA schedule.


Qualifications

  • You have successfully designed and shipped mesh networking protocols in commercial or defence products.
  • Deep, practical familiarity with the Linux networking stack at the kernel and packet levels, coupled with strong live-debugging skills on embedded systems.
  • Strong understanding of wireless propagation and physical layer realities, with hands-on experience designing medium-access control schemes or TDMA schedulers.


Nice to have

  • Active contributions to open-source routing protocols (e.g., batman-adv, olsrd, Babel).
  • A professional background at tactical mesh vendors (such as Silvus, Persistent Systems, TrellisWare, Saab, or Bittium).
  • Experience with mmWave backhaul systems or other technologies where directional beamforming is the default mode of operation.
  • Batman-adv / olsrd / Babel contributor; tactical mesh vendor background (Silvus, Persistent, TrellisWare, Saab, Bittium); mmWave backhaul — already thinks in beams.

L’Université de Picardie Jules Verne (UPJV) est un établissement public à caractère scientifique, culturel et professionnel (EPSCP) qui accueille près de 32 000 étudiants en formation initiale ou continue.

Elle développe des formations professionnalisantes désormais pleinement reconnues sur le marché du travail. L'excellence des équipes de recherche est reconnue au plan régional, national et international. Les unités de recherche de l'UPJV sont impliquées dans trois champs disciplinaires que sont les sciences (12 unités de recherche), la santé (11 unités de recherche) et les sciences humaines et sociales (13 unités de recherche). Dans chacun de ces trois champs, les compétences des différents laboratoires sont organisées autour de thématiques fédératrices assurant la lisibilité de l’offre de recherche de l’UPJV.

L’UPJV est membre du consortium européen BAUHAUS4EU – A European University for Resilient, Sustainable, Inclusive and Beautiful Regions. Cette alliance européenne concerne plus de 124 000 étudiants et 10 000 personnels dans 10 universités issues de 9 pays. En effet, en plus de l’UPJV, un second partenaire français, l’Université Lumière Lyon 2 (ULL2) figure dans l’alliance. L’ingénieur.e pédagogique recruté.e sera amené.e à fonctionner en binôme avec son homologue lyonnais.e (recrutement à venir).

L’entreprise

Depuis 2020, Elax Energie propose de réaliser des économies d’énergie et de la flexibilité sur le réseau électrique pour une consommation plus verte ♻️

Concrètement, Elax a développé un boîtier (fabriqué en France 🇫🇷) qui pilote à distance des chauffe-eaux existants afin de réduire la consommation des logements sociaux et les faire consommer quand l’électricité est moins carbonée sur le réseau.

Elax, c’est :

⚡️Déjà + de 80 000 boîtiers installés

⚡️ +90 bailleurs sociaux conquis par la solution

⚡️ 20% d’économies d’énergie réalisées en moyenne

⚡️ +de 50 super Elaxians motivés (et ce n’est que le début !)

En 2026, nous poursuivons notre ascension en recrutant nos postes-clés afin de développer de nouvelles verticales et renforcer notre super team !

Convaincus qu’une politique humaine est essentielle à l’épanouissement de nos Elaxians, nous veillons à faire vivre nos valeurs au coeur de nos actions quotidiennes.

Ta future équipe

Tu rejoindras la Squad Apps, composée de 4 développeurs seniors qui travaillent sur l’ensemble des applications Elax : application mobile et web pour les résidents, outils à destination des bailleurs, back-office interne et Elax Pro, la plateforme dédiée aux plombiers.

Il y a une répartition par projet/domaine métier :

  • Hugo travaille sur Elax Pro ainsi que sur les sujets organisationnels/process internes.

  • Gauthier travaille sur le back-office et son lien avec Salesforce qui représente pratiquement un an d’harmonisation technique.

  • Christophe est dédié à l’application destinée aux locataire et possède la casquette de référent sur de nombreux sujets d’architecture technique.

  • Quant à Nils, il est positionné sur les outils bailleurs sociaux.

Chaque membre de l’équipe est garant de son domaine projet mais toute l’équipe travaille ensemble pour harmoniser le système technique. Nous avons besoin de toi pour encadrer tout cela, prendre de la hauteur de vue et avoir une vue transversale sur l’ensemble des projets/produits Elax.

Le poste est donc une création de poste : tu prendras le management direct des quatre développeurs et tu deviendras le point de repère de l’équipe sur les sujets humains, organisationnels et delivery.

Tu seras rattaché.e à Florent Pignal, CTO, et tu travailleras en étroite collaboration avec Christophe, référent architecture et technique, ainsi qu’avec Hugo, aujourd’hui moteur sur les rituels et l’amélioration continue. Hugo va progressivement se recentrer sur Elax Pro, ce qui te permettra de reprendre pleinement le rôle de Team Lead de la Squad Apps.

Tes missions

Afin de donner à la Squad Apps le cadre, le soutien et le rythme nécessaires pour continuer à grandir, nous recherchons notre futur.e Team Lead.

Ton rôle sera partagé entre 60 % de contribution individuelle et 40 % de management et d’amélioration continue. L’objectif : rester dans le code tout en faisant progresser les personnes, les pratiques et la capacité de delivery de l’équipe.

Dans le détail, tes missions serons les suivantes :

1 - Faire grandir les personnes et fédérer l’équipe

Tu seras le manager direct des quatre développeurs de la squad. À ce titre, tu :

  • Organiseras des 1:1 réguliers, accompagneras la progression individuelle et donneras des feedbacks utiles, y compris lorsque les conversations sont difficiles.

  • Fixeras et suivras les objectifs, mèneras les entretiens semestriels et annuels et identifieras les besoins de formation ou de montée en compétence.

  • Contribueras à maintenir le lien dans une équipe qui travaille aujourd’hui davantage par projets, en favorisant l’entraide, le partage de connaissances et la collaboration.

Tu seras un véritable servant leader : là pour donner du contexte, faciliter les décisions, tirer l’équipe vers le haut et créer les conditions de sa réussite, pas pour imposer sans discussion.

2 - Structurer le delivery et porter l’amélioration continue

Tu prendras le rôle de Team Lead sur les sujets d’organisation et de fonctionnement collectif. Cela signifie, concrètement, que tu :

  • Animeras les rituels de l’équipe : daily, rétrospectives, points de synchronisation et temps de partage.

  • Amélioreras progressivement la gestion des tickets, le découpage du backlog, la priorisation et la visibilité sur le delivery.

  • Mesureras et réduiras le temps consacré au run, avec un objectif de le ramener sous les 15 % du temps de l’équipe.

  • Mettras en place des process légers, utiles et adaptés à la réalité de la squad, sans créer de bureaucratie inutile.

Tu favoriseras le travail de tous les membres de l’équipe avec le produit et le métier avec le produit et le métier pour clarifier les besoins, faciliter les arbitrages et rendre les contraintes techniques compréhensibles par tous. Tu donneras le rythme, tu anticiperas les éventuels blocage dans la roadmap et tu sauras trancher.

3 - Continuer à produire du code de qualité

Tu resteras pleinement dans la mêlée. Environ 60 % de ton temps sera consacré à la contribution individuelle, notamment :

  • Prendre en charge des tickets et des EPICs sur les différents projets de la squad.

  • Concevoir, développer et contribuer aux choix d’architecture.

  • Effectuer des revues de code et maintenir un haut niveau d’exigence sur la qualité.

  • Apporter une vision globale sur les applications Elax tout en gardant les mains dans le code.

Christophe restera le référent architecture et backlog technique. Vous travaillerez ensemble sur les priorités techniques, les sujets de dette, les performances et les arbitrages avec le produit.

C’est un rôle à deux têtes : d’un côté tu es le chef d’orchestre organisationnel avec un rôle de manager d’équipe et de l’autre tu fais partie de la mêlée pour aider, débloquer des situations complexes, prendre des tickets et mettre les mains dans le cambouis.

Tes objectifs à horizon 1 an

Phase 1 (0 à 3 mois) : embarquement et premiers quick-wins

  • Comprendre les produits, l’architecture, les enjeux métier et le fonctionnement de la squad.

  • Créer la relation avec les quatre développeurs et installer tes rituels de management.

  • Prendre en main les premiers tickets et sujets techniques.

  • Identifier les irritants prioritaires et lancer quelques améliorations simples sur le delivery

Phase 2 (3 à 6 mois) - montée en puissance et autonomie

  • Être pleinement autonome dans le management de l’équipe.

  • Reprendre le lien quotidien avec le produit et le métier.

  • Apporter d’éventuelles modification aux rituels, à la gestion du backlog et donner de la visibilité sur le delivery, en discussion avec l’équipe.

  • Trouver le bon équilibre entre contribution individuelle, management et amélioration continue.

Phase 3 (6 à 12 mois) - maitrise et apport stratégique

  • Permettre au CTO de ne plus manager directement les développeurs de la squad.

  • Faire fonctionner les rituels et les process de l’équipe de manière autonome.

  • Ramener le run sous les 15 % du temps de l’équipe.

  • Maîtriser le lead time des EPICs: le temps entre “le début et la fin des travaux techniques”

  • Continuer à contribuer au code tout en apportant une vraie valeur stratégique sur les produits et l’organisation technique.

🔎 Profil recherché

Nous recherchons un profil Senior ou Intermédiaire confirmé, avec une première expérience réelle du management d’équipe (N+1 hiérarchique ou posture mentor/coach d’équipe) . Tu peux avoir environ 7 à 8 ans d’expérience, ou moins si tu as déjà 1 à 2 ans de management concret.

Ce poste n’est pas un premier poste de manager : nous attendons que tu aies déjà accompagné des personnes, fixé des objectifs et porté des feedbacks.

Le point essentiel : tu dois aimer les deux dimensions du rôle. Nous ne cherchons ni un manager qui ne code plus, ni un excellent développeur qui vivrait les 1:1 comme une contrainte.

Hard skills

  • Très bon niveau en développement fullstack JavaScript/TypeScript, avec une expérience solide sur React et Node.js.

  • Expérience récente de contribution au code en production, de revue de code et de conception technique.

  • Capacité à découper et prioriser un backlog, animer des rituels et améliorer un process de delivery.

  • Expérience concrète de l’usage de l’IA dans le quotidien d’une équipe : plusieurs usages intégrés, recul critique sur les limites et impact observable.

  • Très apprécié: une expérience pratique d’application des principes Lean dans une équipe Tech.

Soft skills

  • Tu as envie de manager des personnes : coaching, progression, objectifs, feedback et conversations difficiles ne te font pas peur. Tu disposes d’un bon sens relationnel et tu sais instaurer une bonne sécurité psychologique dans l’équipe.

  • Tu sais manager des profils plus expérimentés que toi sur leur spécialité, avec humilité, clarté et suffisamment de leadership pour faire avancer les décisions.

  • Tu es pragmatique, autonome et orienté.e résultats. Tu sais instaurer un cadre sans alourdir le quotidien et tu identifies les signaux faibles avant qu’ils ne deviennent des problèmes.

  • Tu aimes débattre, écouter, arbitrer et construire avec les autres.

Les points de mismatch :

  • Posture 100 % manageriale, pas assez hands-on

  • Absence d’expérience préalable en encadrement : il faut avoir sué un peu du front sur des enjeux humains et organisationnels et avoir de bons réflexes sans se laisser déborder par la situation.

  • Posture de management autoritaire ou décision unilatérale sans concertation. L’équipe tech Elax fonctionne grandement dans la coopération, l’alignement des visions et des objectifs. Il y a une culture du débat, du désaccord et un droit à l’erreur.

  • Posture dogmatique : “c’est ainsi et pas autrement”. Elax est une jeune entreprise avec une roadmap et des priorités qui changent. Il est important de composer avec des incertitudes, des changements technologiques ce qui exige une belle ouverture d’esprit.

Chez Elax, l’IA fait partie intégrante de notre quotidien. Nous recherchons des talents curieux, prêts à explorer ces technologies et à faire évoluer leurs méthodes de travail à nos côtés.

Ce que nous te proposons

💶 Salaire : 63K€ à 77K€ bruts annuels selon ton expérience et ton niveau de contribution.

📈 Un poste clé au cœur d’une start-up en pleine croissance, avec un vrai impact sur l’équipe, les produits et l’organisation Engineering.

Search Atlas | Product Engineer (Product Manager role, not a Full-stack role) | REMOTE (anywhere, EST hours) | Full-time contractor | $23-$34 USD/hour | https://careers.searchatlas.com/jobs/599248-product-engineer...

We're ~160 people, fully remote, building an AI marketing platform. Our main product is OTTO, which runs a site's SEO on its own - it reads live search data and pushes the technical and on-page fixes itself, nobody queues them up. Around that we've got ad automation for Google and Meta, GBP management for multi-location brands, content gen, and LLM visibility tracking (whether ChatGPT and co are citing you). Autotrader, Hyundai, P&G, Vendasta are some of our customers.

Work happens in pods, 1 PM and 2-4 engineers. You own your pod's roadmap and ship it with them, no veteran PM signing off on your specs first. That's the part most PM roles won't hand you.

Looking for 3+ years PM in B2B SaaS with an actual technical background - eng or QA before PM, or a PM who's been getting into the codebase themselves. You should be able to read Python and TS, write your own SQL, find your way around an API, and not need an engineer to tell you what a stack trace says. We're Django on the back, React/Next on the front. QA is yours end to end including release sign-off, people tend to underestimate that bit. And you're already using Claude Code or similar daily, not "open to it".

Process is screen with me, a take-home that runs about 75 mins, technical round with one of our senior PMs, then a call with our Director of Product (who you'd report to). I usually come back to people within 2 business days.

Our ATS forces us to list specific countries but we hire from anywhere as long as you can do EST hours, so apply even if yours isn't on there.

Apply at the link and mention HN somewhere, in your pitch or wherever it fits. I'm João Pedro, I read all of your emails. joao.pedro@searchatlas.com if you need me, though the link's faster.

P.S: If you're not a PM, you can still reach out, explain your role briefly and I can redirect you to an appropriate role, or you could just check out our careers page and apply directly to the role that suits you best (preferred method).
